sentences.text:
Challenging the award dated 16/02/2018 passed by the 2nd Additional Motor Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:16786 Accident Claims Tribunal, Raigarh (CG) in MACT No.48/2017, the appellants /
claimants have filed this appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'MV Act').

entities.text: 2nd Additional Motor Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:16786 Accident Claims Tribunal, Raigarh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. By the impugned award, against a claim of Rs.45,00,000/-, learned Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.11,89,000/- in favour of the appellants / claimants on account of death of Navratan Patel in an accident that occurred on 11/04/2017 by rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle (Oil Tanker) bearing registration No.CG-10 R-1164 by respondent No.1 / driver,
owned by respondent No.2 and insured with respondent No.3/insurance company.
3. As per pleadings of the claim application, at the time of accident, the deceased was aged about 42 years.
He was operating an auto parts shop and was earning Rs.20,000/- monthly.
Therefore, the aforesaid compensation was claimed.
The appellants / claimants are parents, widow and minor children of the deceased.
Respondents 1 and 2 remained ex-parte before the Tribunal and the insurance company took a plea that there was violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
4. On the basis of above broad pleadings, learned Tribunal framed issues, decided those issues in favour of the appellants / claimants and awarded the aforestated compensation.
5. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the monthly income of the deceased has been taken on lower side and amount awarded on other heads is also on the lower side.
Therefore, it is prayed that suitable enhancement may be made.
6. Learned counsel for respondent No.3 supports the award and submits that just compensation has been awarded and no interference is called for.
He submits that the insurance company has filed a cross -objection on the ground that no document was filed with regard to occupation of the deceased and excess amount has been awarded.
7. I have heard learned counsel for the parties, considered their rival submissions Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:16786 and perused the records.

8. So far as objection of the insurance company with regard to assessment of income is concerned,
learned Tribunal has found the monthly income of the deceased to Rs.9750/- as per the minimum rate prescribed by the Labour Commissioner for unskilled labour in then notification of the CG Govt. which does not require any interference.
Hence, the contention of counsel for respondent No.3 is rejected.
Consequently, cross-objection is also rejected.

9. Considering the age of the deceased, number of dependents, evidence *-
available and minimum wages prevailing, the monthly income of the deceased is taken to Rs.9750/-
and taking guidance from the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation and ors., (2009) 6 SCC 121, National Insurance Co. Ltd. v.

The learned Tribunal has awarded Rs.11,89,000/- which is deducted from the total compensation now awarded and the enhanced compensation comes to Rs.5,76,562/-.

Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, interest @ 6% is also awarded on the enhanced amount of compensation from the date of this order to be deposited by the insurance company within a period of 60 days.
After the amount of compensation is deposited, learned Tribunal shall pass appropriate order with regard to apportionment, investment and disbursement.
11. The appeal thus allowed in part.
